title: Release pipeline — immutable versioned assets, a stable manifest pointer, smoke tests and rollback

tasks.title: Storage targets, publish, smoke, promote and rollback
release.yml on merge to main, with secret-gated real steps
Local release and rollback, end to end through the harness

acs.text: WHEN `release publish` runs on a surface build THE SYSTEM SHALL check every file the manifest lists against its integrity hash, upload each file and then the manifest under `v/<version>/` with immutable cache headers, never upload source maps, refuse to replace an existing file of that version with different bytes, and treat a re-run with the same bytes as done
scenarios: AC-001 publish uploads a version immutably
AC-001 publish refuses a build whose file does not match its hash

acs.text: WHEN `release promote <version>` runs THE SYSTEM SHALL first smoke-test the published version (the manifest validates against the reader's pinned schema, its contract major is served, every file read back matches its hash), then write `stable/manifest.json` with the same entries pointing into `v/<version>/` and a no-cache header, and keep the previous stable version as the last known-good; a version that is not published, fails the smoke test or was rolled back is refused and the pointer does not move
scenarios: AC-002 promote smoke-tests and moves the pointer
AC-002 promote refuses a bad version

acs.text: WHEN `scripts/rollback` runs with no argument THE SYSTEM SHALL move the stable pointer to the last known-good version and mark the version it replaced as rolled back; WITH a version argument it SHALL move to that version if it is a known-good one; WHEN there is no known-good version it SHALL refuse and leave the pointer as it was
scenarios: AC-003 rollback moves the pointer back
AC-003 rollback with nothing to go back to

acs.text: WHEN `RELEASE_TARGET` is `file:<dir>` THE SYSTEM SHALL use that folder as the storage target; WHEN it is `bucket:<name>` THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse with a message that the object-store target is a stub until the hosting exists; WHEN it is unset or unknown THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse and say how to set it

WHEN a commit lands on main THE SYSTEM SHALL run `release.yml`: build and budget-check the surface, rehearse publish, promote and rollback against a filesystem target, then upload, deploy the server, smoke-test and promote for real, each real step skipping with a notice naming the missing secret or variable when it is absent; release runs never cancel each other; a manual run can roll back

WHEN two versions are released to a filesystem target served over HTTP and the harness loads the stable manifest the way the reader does (origin allowlist, integrity on every file) THE SYSTEM SHALL load the second version, after rollback load the first version again, and refuse to load a version whose published file was altered
scenarios: AC-006 a local release and rollback, end to end
